source.public_versification_note: Public Joshua 1–8 and Hebrew source references align one to one. All 186 original source records are bound exactly once.

key_decisions.decision: Preserves the movement from Israel’s collective breach to Achan’s act and back to divine anger against Israel; keeps the full lineage.
Keeps approximate casualties, the uncertain place name, and the heart-to-water image that reverses the enemy’s fear.
Retains Joshua’s accusatory question and wish without correcting or softening his protest.
Retains the accumulating charges and collective pronouns instead of limiting the divine indictment to Achan.
Keeps the corporate herem reversal and conditional withdrawal of presence with the repeated destruction term.
Makes the narrowing sequence clear without inserting an unmentioned physical lot procedure.
Preserves the burning, encompassing scope, covenant offense, and outrage without prematurely restricting its referents.
Preserves the actual man-by-man wording rather than harmonizing this stage with verse 14’s household instruction.
Retains the familial address and glory/confession idiom while making the demand for disclosure plain.
Preserves saw/coveted/took, Shinar, both weights, and the gold-tongue image; leaves underneath’s precise object for the note.
Preserves children, animals, possessions, collective participation, and the shortened ancestry as written; assigns no unstated guilt to the children.
Keeps the shift from singular him to plural them and the narrated order instead of harmonizing away the punishment’s troubling scope.
Preserves the return to singular him, double to-this-day notices, and trouble/Achor wordplay in a note.
